newsitem.title: USA: Ultramar Diamond sets $811 mln TOPNA buy.
newsitem.headline: Ultramar Diamond sets $811 mln TOPNA buy.

text.p: Ultramar Diamond Shamrock Corp and Total Petroleum (North America) Ltd. said Tuesday that they had agreed that Ultramar would acquire Total Petroleum for stock in a deal which values it at $811 million, including $414 million in debt.
Total Petroleum shareholders will receive 0.322 Ultramar shares for each of their own shares, the companies said.

The deal, which has been flagged for some time, has yet to be ratified by shareholders, but the companies said that France's Total S.A., which owns 55.5 percent of Total Petroleum shares, will vote in favour of the deal.
They expect the deal to close in the summer and estimate annual savings and synergies at $50 million.

"The acquisition of Total Petroleum, with its refining and distribution system and high-quality gasoline and convenience store outlets, is another step in our plans to strategically grow refining, supply and marketing," said UDS chief executive Roger Hemminghaus.
The deal will add 150,000 barrels per day of refining capacity to Ultramar Diamond Shamrock, bringing the total to 650,000 barrels of oil per day.
Ultramar said that would run the Total Petroleum facilities with two million barrels less crude oil, feedstock and refined product inventories.

The merged company will have 6,381 branded outlets in 19 states and six Canadian provinces, 5,679 miles of crude oil and refined products pipelines, and over 23,000 employees. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
